transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you here today?

Well... I guess the thing that finally got me in here is the eating. It’s hard to explain without sounding foolish at my age, but once I start, it’s like my hands just keep going back for more, even while I’m telling myself, “Tom, stop this right now.” And I mean it, I really do, but it doesn’t feel like I’m in charge in that moment.

I used to have better discipline, you know. My father was strict about that sort of thing—clean plate, no fussing—and I worked hard most of my life, kept routines. But lately, or maybe not lately exactly, it’s just... that feeling of not being able to stop is what scares me most.
After these episodes of eating more than you intend to, do you ever try to compensate for it by doing things like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

Yes... yes, I have. Not every time, but there are times after I’ve eaten too much where I go into the bathroom and make myself bring it back up.

It’s embarrassing to say that out loud. My mother used to say you shouldn’t waste food, you know, and that sticks with you, even at my age. But then I get scared it’s just going to stay in me, like I’ve done some damage I can’t undo. So I’ve taken laxatives too, for the same reason. I don’t like admitting that.
Do these episodes of eating more than you intend tend to happen more often when you're feeling stressed, upset, or dealing with something emotionally difficult?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I suppose everybody eats differently when they’re upset, don’t they? My wife used to bake when the house was tense, and then of course there’d be cakes sitting around, and that never helped anybody.

But for me… I haven’t really kept track of whether it’s stress or not. Sometimes it just seems to happen, and afterward I sit there thinking, “What was that about?” Maybe there’s something underneath it, but I couldn’t tell you straight off.
How often would you say these episodes of eating more than you intend happen—like, how many times a week or month?

I started keeping little food logs—my daughter said it might help, though I used to keep better records back when I was working, everything in neat columns, you know. Anyway… looking at those, it’s been many months now, and nearly every week there’s at least one afternoon where I just lose control with the eating.

And then afterward I try to make up for it somehow—sometimes being sick, sometimes laxatives, or I’ll skip food, or push myself walking and doing chores longer than I should. So… I’d say at least weekly, most weeks.
Do you find yourself particularly worried about your weight or the shape of your body, or do you feel like you’ve gained weight even if others might not notice it?

Yes… yes, I do worry about it. More than I should, I suppose.

It’s silly, because my doctor keeps telling me I’m too thin, and he’s got the chart and the little printout and all that. But if I step on the scale and it’s up even half a pound, I feel this awful panic, like I’ve let myself go. Ashamed, really. Like I have to do something about it right away.

I know half a pound could be anything—water, shoes, whatever—but in my head it doesn’t feel like that. It feels like I’ve failed.
Do you usually eat this way when you're alone, or do you find yourself doing this even when others are around?

Mostly when I’m alone, yes. If someone’s around, I can act normal enough, have a cup of tea or a proper sandwich, that sort of thing.

But those afternoons at the house by myself… that’s when it happens. I’ll start with toast or something small, and then somehow I’ve gone through a loaf of bread, peanut butter, cookies, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, even ice cream, all in one sitting before I really look up.

It sounds ridiculous saying it out loud. I don’t think I’d do that with someone sitting there watching me.

When these episodes happen, would you say you're eating a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in one sitting, or does it feel more like a normal or slightly larger than normal amount to you?

It’s… it’s much more than a normal sitting, I think. I mean, I don’t like admitting that, but on those afternoons when I’m alone in the house, I can go through a whole loaf of bread, peanut butter, cookies, whatever leftovers are in the fridge… and then ice cream too, all before I really even look up.

It’s not like a second helping at supper, you know. It’s… a lot.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're not in control of your eating, like you can't stop yourself even if you want to?

Yes… that’s the frightening part, really. Once I start, it’s like my hands just keep going back for more, even while I’m saying to myself, “Tom, stop this now.”

And I’ll mean it, too. It’s not like I’m enjoying it in some simple way. I’ll be standing there at the counter, or going back to the cupboard, and thinking I should stop, I should put it away… but then I’m reaching again. Funny, my wife used to say I was always careful with things in the kitchen, never wasted a crumb, and now— well. Yes. I don’t feel in control of it when it’s happening.
Can you describe what goes through your mind during these episodes? Specifically, do you feel like you’re not in control of your actions, even though you want to stop?

Yes… yes, that’s exactly it. What scares me most is that once I start eating, it feels like my hands just keep reaching for more, even while I’m telling myself, “Tom, stop this right now.”

It’s a strange thing, because I’ve always thought of myself as fairly disciplined—well, my father used to say if you start a job, you finish it properly, and I suppose that stuck with me. But in those moments, it’s like that part of me isn’t in charge. I know I want to stop, I’m saying it in my head, and still I’m reaching again.
